iDiv Conference · Jena · 2026
R Environment for
Environmental Sciences
Many ecological analyses cannot be re-run two years later, or trusted if they can. These four packages fix four reasons why.
Alban Sagouis · Scientific Programmer, iDiv
Looking for my next
adventure, let's talk
Reproducibility is not one tool, it's a sequence.
01
renv
Locked environments
PROBLEM
Your whole analysis runs today. In two years, after silent package updates and a move to another server, it won't. No record of what it depends on, no versions, no way back.
SOLUTION
renv gives each project its own package library and records every version in renv.lock. One call restores the exact environment, anywhere, anytime, including from Zenodo five years on.
KEY FUNCTIONS
init()
snapshot()
restore()
02
pins
Shared, versioned data
PROBLEM
You clean a dataset, need it in four places, email it around, it gets updated, and months later nobody knows which version was used.
SOLUTION
pins keeps one canonical copy on a shared board locally, on the iDiv server or online. One URL, always current, versioned so you can roll back. pin_read() is the same call on every machine.
KEY FUNCTIONS
pin_write()
pin_read()
pin_versions()
03
testthat
Verified assumptions
PROBLEM
A function silently renames a column. Your pipeline drops 300 rows, and nothing errors. You find out at submission, three months after the pipeline ran.
SOLUTION
Write expectations in code: column names, value ranges, and no duplicates, checked at every step. checkmate adds compact argument checks; testdat adds data-frame assertions.
KEY FUNCTIONS
expect_numeric()
expect_identical()
expect_type()
04
rmarkdown
Code and prose, in sync
PROBLEM
The figure came from analysis_FINAL_v3_USE_THIS.R. Which parameters? Six months ago, it was obvious.
SOLUTION
rmarkdown keeps code, output, and prose in one document: change the code and every number and figure follows. Quarto adds journal templates and cross-references, and turns the same file into a website, book, or talk.
KEY FUNCTIONS
render()
word_document()
pdf_document()
THE WORKFLOW: ALL FOUR, ONCE
# 1. locked environment ─────── renv

renv::init()

# 2. shared data ────────────── pins
board <- pins::board_connect()
fish  <- pins::pin_read(board, "fish_cleaned")

# 3. validate ───────────────── testthat

testthat::expect_identical(ncol(fish), 8L)
checkmate::assert_data_frame(fish, min.rows = 100L)

# 4. report ─────────────────── rmarkdown

rmarkdown::render("fish_report.Rmd") # in sync
